_source: diagnostics/seird_split_artifact/run_3trial_protocol.py, run on CPU (verified 2026-08-24). Uses a REPRESENTATIVE (random) 70/15/15 train/val/test split instead of the chronological split the original benchmark used (see results/seird_symfm_results_chronological_split.json for that run, which reported a saturated L2_mean=10.0 at every N). The chronological split placed the test window entirely in the post-epidemic near-zero-derivative tail of these single-wave SEIRD trajectories, which destabilizes the relative-L2 metric independent of model quality; diagnostics/seird_split_artifact/ has the full writeup and per-trial output. ERR_mean=0.0 at every N under both splits -- exact symbolic recovery (tol=0.25) is genuinely not achieved -- but L2_mean under the representative split is flat at ~0.90-0.91 across N=50/250/500, in the same difficulty range as this repo's hardest Lorenz-96 results, rather than the qualitatively different order-of-magnitude failure the chronological split implied. This file is what the paper's Table 3 SEIRD column is based on as of the 2026-08-24 rebuild.
